title: Guesstimate market size of paneer in Bangalore
persona: Aryan, applying to consulting via campus placements
scenario: Case prep for consulting interviews. Question: ‘Estimate the daily market size of paneer in Bangalore.’ You don't have a phone, can't Google, and your interviewer wants to see the structure of your thinking, not the right answer. You want a worked guesstimate with the population number you assume, the consumption split (veg/non-veg, urban/rural, daily/weekly), the per-capita-per-occasion math, and one assumption you'd flag as the biggest source of error.
badPrompt: estimate the market size of paneer in bangalore
badOutput: Bangalore has approximately 13 million people. Assume 60% are vegetarian, of which 40% consume paneer daily at 50g per person. That gives roughly 156 tonnes per day. The market size is around 156 tonnes daily.

hints.title: Force visible structure
hints.body: ‘Show every assumption as a labelled step. Population → veg-share → daily-consumer-share → per-occasion grams.’ Interviewers grade structure, not answer.

hints.title: Demand a sensitivity flag
hints.body: ‘Name the one assumption that, if wrong by 2x, breaks the answer most.’ This is what separates analyst from estimator.

checks.tip: Frame the artifact, a guesstimate, not a research answer.
Anchor the unit, daily paneer in Bangalore, in kg/tonnes.
Anchor the constraint, no Google, live verbal.
Reference what's being graded, structure of thinking.
Force every assumption shown as a labelled step.
Anchor the segmentation, veg-share, urban/rural, frequency.
Demand a sensitivity flag, the assumption that breaks the answer.
Force a per-capita-per-occasion number, not just population × %.
Specify the structure, numbered steps with assumption + value + source-of-error.
Force a spoken-friendly format, you'll deliver this verbally.

tipIfLow: Guesstimates fail when they jump to a final number. The unlock is forcing visible structure (population → veg → frequency → grams) AND a sensitivity flag on the assumption that breaks the answer most. Interviewers grade reasoning, not your match to the ‘right’ answer.
goldPrompt: Act as a consulting interviewer grading structure, not the answer. I'm Aryan, prepping case interviews. Question: 'Estimate the daily market size of paneer in Bangalore.' No phone, no Google. Output a worked guesstimate as a labelled chain: (1) Bangalore population assumption, (2) veg-share split, (3) daily-consumer share, (4) typical occasion frequency, (5) per-occasion grams, (6) final number in tonnes/day AND ₹/day. Then explicitly name the ONE assumption that, if wrong by 2×, breaks the answer most. Show every multiplication. Don't reach for a 'right' answer — show structure.
